_comment: Wire-format test vectors for application_protocol_v1.md, loaded by both
Neither implementation generated these bytes. Each expected_bytes was
derived by hand from the spec's field layout and IEEE-754, then both
implementations were run against it. Vectors produced by running one codec
would only prove the two agree -- including when they agree on something
wrong, which is the case this file exists to catch.
reading is a JSON number for finite values and one of the strings 'inf',
'-inf', 'nan' otherwise: those three have no JSON number form. Python's
json module emits bare Infinity/NaN, which is not valid JSON and which
nlohmann rejects, so the strings keep this file parseable by both sides.
Maximum-length params (4089 B) is exercised in the round-trip tests rather
than here -- 8 KB of hex would bury the vectors that show a layout.

vectors.name: 0x12 typical: ack requested, two param bytes
0x12 all bits set: no field is masked or clamped
0x12 params are opaque bytes, not text
0x10 seq=256 catches a byte-swapped u16: 0001, not 0100
0x10 seq at the uint16 ceiling, reading 0.0
